title: Wien Consolidated Airlines 55
summary: Fairchild F-27B Flight 55 was at 11,500 ft preparing to approach Iliamna when it encountered extreme turbulence. The aircraft had fatigue cracks in its wings from improper and shoddy maintenance that could not withstand the stresses. The structural failure of the right wing forced the aircraft into a steep, uncontrolled spiral descent that crashed into Pedro Bay.
probable_cause: The accident resulted from structural failure of the right wing due to metal fatigue cracks caused by improper maintenance, combined with extreme turbulence that exceeded the wing's reduced strength.

factors.evidence: fatigue cracks had formed on the aircraft's wings due to improper and shoddy maintenance
a number of fatigue cracks had formed on the aircraft's wings
the aircraft encountered extreme, unreported turbulence with winds in excess of 50 knots at 11,500 ft
the stresses due to turbulence and air pressure caused a structural failure in the aircraft's right wing, forcing it into a spiraling, uncontrollable dive
the aircraft descended in a steep, uncontrolled spiral towards the ground

events.text: Flight 55 departed Anchorage International Airport at 8:46 am bound for Dillingham with stops
First officer Jerry Svengard contacted Iliamna air traffic control to request approach clearance at 9:25 am
Iliamna ATC granted the approach clearance at 9:26 am
While preparing to approach at 11,500 ft the aircraft encountered extreme turbulence
The right wing suffered structural failure, separation of pieces, and the aircraft entered a steep uncontrolled spiral
The aircraft crashed into Foxys Lake at Pedro Bay
